title: Compute fence & burst qualification — Catalyst Dynamics
meeting_header:
Date: 2025-01-17 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 42m
Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Priya Natarajan (Redwood AE), Samir Okafor (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Catalyst CTO), Liam Ortiz (Infra), Roxanne Patel (Security)
summary: High-level qualification for dedicated capacity. Catalyst runs latency-sensitive agent orchestration and wants isolation + burst for peak inference. Discussed reserved GPU sizing, warm-pool/prewarm behaviors, VPC & KMS requirements, latency vs cost tradeoffs and a small bench pilot. Action: Redwood to send tailored pricing, burst model spreadsheet, security pack, and schedule a bench run session.
topics: Burst strategy: warm pools, prewarm, and burst pricing
Compliance: SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): Hey thanks everyone for joining, we really appreciate you taking the time. Quick intros?
[00:12] Maya (Catalyst CTO): Hi, Maya here, CTO at Catalyst Dynamics. We're rebuilding our inference plane to support multi-tenant agents, latency percentiles are key.
[00:22] Samir (Redwood SE): Great, Samir from Redwood infra. We'll focus on dedicated sizing and burst patterns.
[00:32] Liam (Infra): Quick note — we're currently on cloud provider X with k8s, doing inference on rented GPU instances, and the problem is cold start tails.
[00:45] Priya: ok — so primary goals are isolation for compliance and predictable latency during spikes, is that right?
[00:52] Maya: Exactly. We have e-commerce bot traffic that spikes up to 6x during promos, and we need p95 under 280ms for generation tasks.
[01:05] Roxanne (Security): From security side, we need VPC peering or private link, KMS for key rotation, and an audit trail we can push into our SIEM. SOC2 is table-stakes.
[01:18] Samir: Understood. On dedicated we can provision reserved GPU pools with tenant fencing or single-tenant nodes. There's tradeoffs: stronger isolation increases cost but reduces noisy-neighbor variance.
[01:33] Priya: curious about your current RPS and model sizes — Maya, can you share rough numbers?
[01:40] Maya: Avg qps is 80 across all endpoints, burst to 500 qps for 10-15 minutes during peaks. Models are 7B and a custom 13B fine-tuned for our domain. Sequence lengths average 512 tokens, some runs go to 2k.
[02:00] Samir: ok 13B at 2k is heavy. For reserved nodes we'd size on the 13B peak path. Two approaches: a pool of dedicated GPUs sized for baseline plus warm-pool headroom, or strong isolation with per-tenant reserved capacity and a burst allowance.
[02:18] Liam: What's the difference practically? I.e., do we pay for the whole warm pool even when idle?
[02:24] Samir: There are options — reserved capacity (monthly commit) and burst credits for temporary overage. Warm-pool prewarm is cheaper if you accept shared warm nodes vs fully single-tenant nodes. Prewarm keeps KV cache hot — reduces cold p95 a lot.
[02:40] Maya: KV cash?
[02:42] Priya: KV cache, as in the key-value cache for autoregressive decoding, yeah — when that's warm you avoid loading large context.
[02:49] Roxanne: How does data plane encryption work? We need customer-managed keys or HSM?
[02:56] Samir: We support KMS integrations and HSM-backed flows in Private deployments; in Dedicated we offer KMS integration with BYOK and audit logs pushed to your syslog.
[03:08] Maya: For compliance we'd prefer BYOK and a private control plane — is that a Private deployment or can Dedicated do the same?
[03:16] Priya: Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated) gives isolation and reserved GPUs, but the control plane is hosted; Private offers a customer-managed control plane and on-prem pattern. If BYOK + fully air-gapped is required, Private is the path. Dedicated can meet most enterprise encryption requirements with KMS + VPC though.
[03:34] Liam: Latency — you mentioned prewarm reduces p95. By how much in practice?
[03:40] Samir: Based on similar workloads, prewarm + KV caching can cut cold-tail p95 from ~800-1,200ms to sub-300ms for the same model and seq length, assuming warm pool coverage is good. But this depends on tokenization and batching patterns.
[03:58] Maya: Ok we need numbers for our traffic — can Redwood run a bench?
[04:02] Priya: Yes, we can do a 48hr bench: simulate your qps distribution, both baseline and spikes. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, token cost and effective warm-pool hit rates.
[04:13] Roxanne: And security sign-off — we'll need SOC2 docs, penetration test summary, and SAML SSO support.
[04:21] Samir: We have a security pack; we'll share SOC2 report redacted, SSO SAML FAQs, and steps for KMS integration.
[04:29] Liam: Pricing question — the reserve commit plus burst credits model: what's the rough math? Pay fixed for reserved GPUs and then per-minute burst?
[04:37] Priya: Typical model: monthly reserved commitment priced by GPU-slot (e.g., x per A100-month equivalent), plus burst usage billed at a premium per token or per GPU-hour. We also offer billing caps and alerts. We'll send a spreadsheet that models your 80->500 qps spikes with different warm pool sizes.
[04:56] Maya: Who's the contact for the bench and pricing?
[04:59] Priya: Me — I'll own the commercial share; Samir will run the bench and be SE contact.
[05:05] Maya: Timeline — we want a pilot in 3 weeks and production in 10-12 weeks if bench looks good.
[05:12] Priya: Sounds feasible. Any hard blockers?
[05:15] Roxanne: Data residency — some datasets must stay in EU — can we localize?
[05:20] Samir: Yes. Dedicated capacity can be region pinned; Private supports on-prem or EU region control plane. We'll note data residency rules in the security pack.
[05:29] Liam: What about autoscaling? If we have reserved nodes but sudden 6x spikes, does Redwood scale instantly?
[05:36] Samir: Autoscaling has two tiers: instant warm-pool spill (if you have warm-pool headroom) and autoscale spin-up which can take minutes depending on image/prefetch. For instant we recommend a warm-pool sized to cover typical burst percentiles and then monitored scaling for larger anomalies.
[05:55] Priya: Any concerns about preemption or preemption of GPU nodes in Dedicated?
[05:58] Samir: Reserved Dedicated nodes are not preemptible. If you use cloud spot for bursting we recommend fallback policies. We'll show a fallback policy: route to slightly smaller model, degraded latency SLO, or queued requests with retry.
[06:13] Maya: Regarding models — we plan to experiment with quantized weights. Is Redwood supporting 4-bit/8-bit quantized variants and how that affects throughput?
[06:20] Samir: Yes, runtime supports int4/int8 profiles and will recommend quantization based on quality/regression testing. Quantization improves throughput but can impact some instruction-level latencies — we'll include model-specific perf estimates in the bench.
[06:34] Roxanne: Audit logs — we need immutable logs with retention controls. Can't have logs truncated before 90 days.
[06:42] Samir: We support configurable retention and can integrate with your SIEM. For Private deployments you control retention entirely.
[06:50] Liam: Is there an SLA for p95?
[06:53] Priya: For Dedicated we offer latency SLOs in contracts for certain tiers — we'll include suggested targets and failure/reroute behaviors in the proposal.
[07:03] Maya: One operational question: how do we debug noisy neighbors if we do shared warm pools?
[07:08] Samir: Console exposes per-request traces, token-level cost breakdown, and model-level latency heatmaps. You can set tenant-level quotas and throttles.
[07:20] Liam: For the bench, what telemetry do you need from our side?
[07:23] Samir: A short sample of request payloads, distribution histogram for qps, typical sequence lengths, and a small prompt corpus. We'll simulate traffic — anonymize PII before sharing.
[07:34] Maya: Ok we'll prepare that.
[07:36] Priya: To recap, Redwood will: share security pack, provide dedicated pricing + burst spreadsheet, run a 48hr bench simulating your traffic, and propose a warm-pool sizing recommendation. Customer to share sample payloads and spike histogram.
[07:54] Roxanne: Sounds good. One more: any reference customers with similar regulated needs?
[07:58] Priya: We can share a redacted reference list — I've had similar engagements with health and fintech customers; I'll include short case notes.
[08:07] Maya: Great.
[08:09] Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the bench kickoff and the pricing doc.
[08:15] (meeting ends)
